checks.result: J_ij=∂_j U_i and W a=Ω×a/2 have consistent curl signs. Independent index contraction tests pass.
Direct differentiation of tau and y gives the stated positive collapse and stretching signs; manufactured time-dependent test passes.
Y=y+(C/c_l)e_z removes C; translations of the field U_h(y)=U(y-h e_z) correspond to C_h=C-c_l h. Coordinate-translation wording should specify this convention.
Independent tensor calculation gives div Rm=δ+V·∇δ+tr(J²)+ΔP. The nonzero divergence correction is essential.
Independent manufactured compressible test verifies curl Rm=Rω+δΩ.
Expanding Ω×V=(J-Jᵀ)V and ∇|V|²/2 reproduces Rm, including the C-dependent center.
Dot the vorticity equation with Ω and use ∇|Ω|²=0. Requires a nonzero interior extremum; not a normalization.
Independent symbolic and numerical rescaling tests verify U_a=aU(y/a), P_a=a²P(y/a), C_a=aC. Vorticity amplitude is invariant.
Angular basis differentiation produces both geometric terms. Independent physical-coordinate and cylindrical finite differences agree on off-axis tests.
Proper rotation Q preserves the equations and C e_z; simultaneous transverse parity is the required symmetry.
Cylindrical modes are even; horizontal Cartesian components shift by ±1. Quadratic terms generate higher even frequencies.
Pullback R_-α U(R_α y) is correct. Independent affine average and physical-volume Parseval tests pass. At n=0, sum over ±n must count the zero mode once.
For O e_z=±e_z, Q commutes with O; transform C with the corresponding sign. Velocity is polar and vorticity is axial under reflections.
The explicit seed formula transforms correctly under orthogonal matrices commuting with M, including inversion and z-reflection. These are branch restrictions unless released.
Parity gives odd horizontal and even vertical transverse degrees. Divergence supplies the transverse trace relation; n=2 velocity can be order r.
For smooth Cartesian fields, a scalar angular mode has r^|k| times a smooth function of r². The ±1 component shift gives the stated coupled orders.
Finite smooth representations do not prove derivative convergence of a limiting profile. The listed checks are required numerical evidence, not a theorem of convergence.
S²=S by Q²=I.
Curl commutes with the action of a proper rotation, with determinant factor for an improper one. Hence U=curl(SA) has the required properties.
The product divergence term must be kept; potential envelopes avoid it. Chain rules are with respect to physical coordinates.

These are proposed search branches, not validated completeness claims. A smooth network on compactified directions has integer radial Taylor increments; explicit fractional envelope families add needed powers, while flat remainders can also occur.
No free amplitude of Ω is provided. Canonical translation alone is not a profile symmetry; C allows a coordinate recentering.

A resolved global max gives the stated scale gauge. A fixed-grid or fixed-weight surrogate requires local sensitivity and interior-resolution checks. The proposed pressure-n=2 phase gauge degenerates when that coefficient vanishes, as it does for the initial seed. No P(0) loss was found in the current numerics loss, consistent with its P∞=0 architecture.
J(0) and the sup of Ω are invariant under spatial scaling. Higher derivatives of J scale as a^-k and should not be called invariant without that qualification.

checks.section: 7.1 exact affine family, scalar factor clause
checks.result: v1.1 repairs the scalar-factor error and classifies Q-equivariant homogeneous linear matrices by Cayley-Hamilton. General affine fields also allow an axial constant offset with a compensating linear pressure; the displayed classification should be read as the U=M y family.
v1.1 correctly identifies constant velocity and linear pressure as an exact unforced solution excluded by the target decay and vorticity requirements.
The required distinctions are mathematically appropriate. Check completion separately; no diagnostic list proves the properties automatically.
The homogeneous multiplier vanishes at d=1-1/c_l, giving all stated exponent ranges. This is an assumed matching class, not an exhaustive theorem.
Spherical divergence gives div_S A_T+(d+2)A_r=0; integrate over S² and use d+2≠0.
At degree 2d-1 the multiplier is -1. The formal cascade is a possible hierarchy; an arbitrary exact tail expansion is not proved to contain only those powers.

With the stated derivative decay and d<-1, f=∂i∂j(U_i U_j) has zero total mass and first moments by integration by parts. Both boundary terms for the first moment are O(R^(2d+2)). Decay of U alone without derivative control is insufficient for this argument.

The core exponent is 5c_l-2. For a nonzero angular leading tail the fixed-ball power of tau cancels, local L² requires d>-3/2, and the profile itself need not lie in L² at infinity. Strong matching is an additional hypothesis.

v1.1 correctly requires all p in an interval (0,p1). Independently saved original theorem math/0601060v2 and related note math/0601661v1 agree on that hypothesis; journal attribution is not independently verified here.

With regularity and natural derivative decay, the integrals and signs are justified in research/whole-space-integrals/PROOF.md. Finite-radius quadrature with no analytic tail bound remains a numerical consistency check.

Primary v3 checked. Keep finite-energy plus gradient-growth hypotheses for 2.1; p>max(3c_l,1) for 3.4; nonzero Ω and local outgoing at a zero for 3.8; decay, normalization and finite nodal set in Definition 3.7 for 3.9; axisymmetry and (3.5),(3.8) for 4.5.
v1.1 removes the unsupported quantitative conclusion and asks for a resolved nonzero n=2 signal.
At a zero with Ω≠0, JΩ=SΩ=Ω; trace then gives the stated incoming direction and eigenvalue sum. It is conditional and must not be imposed when Ω=0.
Complete independent proof, including the local null-graph lemma, in research/stagnation-obstruction/PROOF.md. The C² decaying countable-stagnation class is excluded below one half.
A finite root search does not certify countability or exhaust all zeros. No universal quantitative residual floor follows without global compactness and stagnation-structure control.
Same statement as 1.3(d). A numerically refined local extremum is not a global maximum certificate.

Independent curl derivation and symbolic/numerical tests agree. The displayed cylindrical n=2 formula is for the affine core M y; the localized seed has additional radial factors. Its generic tail is asymptotic, not exactly homogeneous at finite radius.
Correctly labeled initializer in the lead file. Direct tests find momentum, vorticity and pressure defects. Its R^(d-2) correction generally fails nonlinear tail balance below one half.
The termwise L² denominator is well defined away from degeneracy. Use physical weights for physical norms. Quantiles/maxima stay sampled quantities. Proposed numeric thresholds are screening choices.
The viscosity coefficient is nu exp[-(1-2c_l)s]. Decay of that coefficient alone establishes no NS singularity.

The independent test suite and synthetic decoder checks pass. Cross-implementation tests are still partial and must be attached to actual checkpoint/source hashes. Numerics test results are its responsibility.

For a nonzero smooth homogeneous leading field of degree -3/2<d<-1, div=0 and curl=0 imply componentwise harmonicity with spherical eigenvalue d(d+1) in (0,3/4), impossible below the first positive eigenvalue 2. See research/irrotational-leading-tail/PROOF.md. Chae does not supply this exclusion, but the angular argument does. Derivative-compatible global angular asymptotics are required.
